pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 1; Q57; question ID 695278282; PDF page 20

articles.title: How can sums of squares give standard deviation?
articles.learningObjective: Recover the sum and sum of squares from shifted-square totals, then calculate variance and standard deviation using divisor n.
articles.example: The numbers 2, 4 and 6, then the same three numbers shifted by 5, show that spread is measured about the mean.
articles.targetQuestionText: For ten numbers x₁, x₂, …, x₁₀, the sum of all (xᵢ + 2)² is 180 and the sum of all (xᵢ − 1)² is 90. What is their standard deviation?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 2; Q8; question ID 695278383; PDF page 3–4
pyqs.independentSolution: Let S=sum x and T=sum x². T+4S+40=180 and T-2S+10=90. Subtraction:6S+30=90, S=10. T=100. Mean=1, variance=100/10-1=9, standard deviation=3.

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 2; Q9; question ID 691121159; PDF page 4
pyqs.independentSolution: Last value is 8n-48. Sum squares is n(16+64)=80n. Thus496+(8n-48)²=80n, giving 4n²-53n+175=0=(n-7)(4n-25). n must be an integer; n=7 and last value=8. Remaining six can satisfy sums48,496 (mean8, variance56/3), so the root is feasible.

review.notes: Use n, not n−1, for the descriptive variance in these JEE questions. Distinguish sum of squares from square of sum; the constant term in each shifted square occurs ten times. articles.title: How do you find a constant term in a binomial?
articles.learningObjective: Find binomial terms by balancing exponents and then calculate their coefficients.
articles.example: Choose how often the second term appears across 18 identical factors.
articles.targetQuestionText: In the expansion of (9x − 1/(3√x))¹⁸ for x > 0, the term independent of x is 221k. What is k?

pyqs.locator: 4 April 2026 Shift 2, Q9, PDF page 4
pyqs.independentSolution: General term C(18,r)(9x)^(18-r)(-1/(3√x))^r. Zero x power requires 18-3r/2=0, so r=12. Numeric factors cancel, leaving C(18,12)=18564=221×84.

pyqs.locator: 5 April 2026 Shift 1, Q23, PDF page 8
pyqs.answer: n=21 with the explicit adapted condition that both terms occur
pyqs.independentSolution: In (x^-3-x^4)^n, exponent is -3n+7r. For x⁷ and x¹⁴, indices r and r+1 exist. Opposite signs and equal magnitude require C(n,r)=C(n,r+1), giving n=2r+1. Also 7r-3n=7, hence n=21, r=10. Caveat: the original question does not explicitly say the coefficients are nonzero; n=1 makes both zero. The adaptation explicitly requires both terms to occur.

pyqs.locator: 4 April 2026, Shift 2, Q30, PDF page 11
pyqs.independentSolution: g(h)/g0 = R²/(R+h)² = 1/9. Positive distances give R+h=3R, so h=2R. Direct check: GM/(3R)² = g0/9.

articles.title: When is a quadratic always positive?
articles.learningObjective: Use the graph and discriminant to test strict positivity, then count allowed coefficient choices; distinguish positive values from positive roots.
articles.example: Raise and lower the parabola y=(x-1)²+k to see crossing, touching and staying above zero.
articles.targetQuestionText: Choose a, b and c independently and equally likely from 1, 2, 3 and 4. The probability that ax² + 2√2 bx + c is positive for every real x is m/n in lowest terms. What is m + n?

pyqs.locator: 2 April 2026, Shift 1, Q23, PDF page 9
pyqs.independentSolution: a,b,c independently uniform in {1,2,3,4}: 64 ordered triples. Since a>0, strict positivity at every real x requires discriminant 8b²-4ac<0, hence ac>2b². For b=1 the allowed c counts by a are 2,3,4,4 =13. For b=2 they are 0,0,2,2 =4. b>=3 impossible since ac<=16<18. Probability17/64, so m+n=81. Independently enumerated all 64 cases.

pyqs.locator: 4 April 2026, Shift 2, Q5, PDF page 2
pyqs.independentSolution: Polynomial (lambda+2)x²-3lambda x+4lambda. Real roots: D=9lambda²-16lambda(lambda+2)=-lambda(7lambda+32)>=0, so -32/7<=lambda<=0. Positive product and sum require lambda/(lambda+2)>0, hence lambda<-2 or lambda>0. Intersection [-32/7,-2), integral values -4,-3; both have strictly positive roots. lambda=0 gives zero roots; lambda=-2 is not quadratic.
